import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clear aesthetic for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a 2x2 subplot grid for a comprehensive dashboard view
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Financial Transaction Analysis', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amounts ---
sns.histplot(data=df, x='amount', kde=True, ax=axes[0, 0], color=sns.color_palette("viridis")[0])
axes[0, 0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amounts', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Amount ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=12)

# --- Plot 2: Transaction Amount by Type ---
# A boxplot shows the distribution, and a stripplot shows individual points
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', ax=axes[0, 1])
sns.stripplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', ax=axes[0, 1], color='black', alpha=0.7, jitter=0.1)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Transaction Amount vs. Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Amount ($)', fontsize=12)

# --- Plot 3: Count of Each Transaction Type ---
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', ax=axes[1, 0], order=df['transaction_type'].value_counts().index)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Frequency of Transaction Types', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=12)
for p in axes[1, 0].patches:
    axes[1, 0].annotate(f'{int(p.get_height())}', (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                        ha='center', va='center', fontsize=12, color='white', xytext=(0, -10),
                        textcoords='offset points', fontweight='bold')

# --- Plot 4: Transaction Amount by Hour of Day ---
# A scatter plot is effective for showing relationships between two numeric variables
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='hour_of_day',
    y='amount',
    hue='transaction_type',
    size='amount',
    sizes=(100, 400),
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    palette='magma',
    legend='auto'
)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Transaction Amount by Hour', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24h)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Amount ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].legend(title='Transaction Details')
axes[1, 1].set_xticks(range(0, 25, 2)) # Set x-ticks for clarity

# Adjust layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the resulting plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

plt.close()
